answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may transact; the stake is slashed if the identity is caught duplicating work or attesting falsely. Forging a thousand hollow identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. A public marble ledger records every stake and slash, so reputation accumulates on one verifiable identity instead of scattering across cheap throwaways, making fakery expensive and honesty profitable.
